summary: Regression test: scripts/targets.sh svc() must not hold a capturing caller's stdout/stderr pipes
prompt:
Write ONE new pytest file, tests/test_targets_sh.py, and nothing else (do not modify scripts/targets.sh or any other file). Use only the project venv (.venv/bin/python, .venv/bin/pytest); do not install packages.

BACKGROUND (the bug this test must catch). scripts/targets.sh starts each target service with its shell function `svc() { # name module port health ... }`. The OLD launch line inside svc() was:

  (cd "$ROOT" && nohup "$PY" -m "$module" --port "$port" >"$RUN/$name.log" 2>&1 & echo $! >"$RUN/$name.pid")

Bash backgrounds the whole `cd && nohup ...` LIST, so it runs in a wrapper bash subshell whose stdout/stderr are still the caller's; the redirection only applies to the nohup command. That wrapper waits for the server forever, so a caller that captures the script's output (scripts/run_e2e_demo.py does `subprocess.run([...targets.sh start --fresh], capture_output=True, timeout=300)`) never sees EOF and hangs until its timeout; also `$!` names the wrapper bash, not the server. The FIXED line (now in scripts/targets.sh) backgrounds only the fully redirected simple command:

  (
    cd "$ROOT"
    nohup "$PY" -m "$module" --port "$port" >"$RUN/$name.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
    echo $! >"$RUN/$name.pid"
  )

WHAT TO WRITE. tests/test_targets_sh.py with a module docstring explaining the above, containing:

1. A helper that reads the script from `Path(os.environ.get("TARGETS_SH") or ROOT / "scripts/targets.sh")` (ROOT = repo root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]) and extracts the complete `svc()` function text with a regex anchored on a line starting `svc() {` up to the first following line that is exactly `}` (re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL); fail with a clear message if it is not found. The TARGETS_SH override is REQUIRED: the acceptance checks run the test against the old script to prove it catches the bug.

2. A fake server program written into tmp_path as an executable file named `fake_target_server.py` with shebang `#!` + sys.executable. It is invoked exactly as svc() invokes $PY: `<fake> -m <module> --port <port>`; it must ignore `-m <module>`, parse `--port`, and serve HTTP on 127.0.0.1:<port> with http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer), answering GET /health with 200 and body ok, logging nothing to stdout except optionally one start line. It runs until killed.

3. test_svc_returns_promptly_with_captured_output_and_records_the_server_pid(tmp_path): build a bash harness string: `set -euo pipefail`, `ROOT=<tmp_path>`, `RUN=<tmp_path>/run`, `mkdir -p "$RUN"`, `PY=<path of fake_target_server.py>`, then the extracted svc() text, then `svc fake fake.module <port> /health`. Use `port = tests.procs.free_port()` (import from tests.procs) — NEVER fixed ports, never 9000-9002. Run it with `subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", harness], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20, start_new_session=True)`. A subprocess.TimeoutExpired must be turned into `pytest.fail("svc() kept the caller's stdout/stderr pipes open (the backgrounded wrapper subshell bug) ...")`. On success assert: returncode 0 and the stdout contains `fake up on :<port>`; the whole call took < 15 s; GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health (httpx, trust_env=False) answers 200; `<tmp_path>/run/fake.pid` holds the pid of the SERVER ITSELF: `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (NUL-separated) contains the fake_target_server.py path and `--port` and str(port), and its argv[0]/argv[1] is not a bash wrapper; `/proc/<pid>/fd/1` and `/proc/<pid>/fd/2` both resolve (os.readlink) to `<tmp_path>/run/fake.log`, and `/proc/<pid>/fd/0` resolves to /dev/null.

4. Cleanup that ALWAYS runs (try/finally or a fixture), also when the test fails or times out under the old idiom: SIGKILL every process whose /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains the unique tmp_path string (this catches the server AND an orphaned wrapper bash), ignoring races (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, FileNotFoundError). After cleanup no process referencing fake_target_server.py from this tmp_path may remain (poll briefly to confirm).

Rules: the test must not write anything outside tmp_path, must not touch .state/, targets/ or the real scripts; keep it fast (< 10 s on success); production-quality, documented code; no network except 127.0.0.1:<free port>. Verify yourself: `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_targets_sh.py` must pass against the current scripts/targets.sh, and `TARGETS_SH=<a copy of scripts/targets.sh where you put the OLD launch line back> .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_targets_sh.py` must FAIL (and leave no fake_target_server.py process behind).
